text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell slightly today despite a strong two-week rally, as oil prices pushed above $100 per barrel on escalating Iran war concerns. The tiny move downward—less than 0.12%—came even as crude climbed and refinery utilization hit 97.8%, suggesting investors may be taking profits after the stock's 10% gain since early September rather than reacting to any new negative catalyst.

The broader refining environment remains supportive: U.S. crude at $97.26 and Brent near $110 create favorable margins for turning crude into gasoline and diesel, and U.S. storage levels for finished products are moderate, which supports steady demand. The stock's strength over two weeks reflects this healthy pricing backdrop, though today's flat-to-down close hints that some of that geopolitical premium may already be priced in.
